prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
For a new central AC or heat-pump installation in Atlanta, I’d call **at least three of these companies** and compare written, like-for-like proposals:

1. **PV Heating, Cooling & Plumbing** — best first call if you want a technically rigorous installation  
   - Strong reputation for **home-performance/building-science** work: correct equipment sizing, duct evaluation, airflow, humidity, and insulation issues—not simply replacing the old unit with the same tonnage.  
   - Particularly worth calling for an **inverter heat pump**, an older/poorly insulated home, comfort problems, hot/cold rooms, or high humidity.  
   - Ask them for a **Manual J load calculation** and duct/airflow recommendations.

2. **Moncrief Heating & Air Conditioning** — strong established option for intown and older Atlanta homes  
   - Long-established Atlanta contractor with broad replacement, maintenance, and system-design capability.  
   - Good company to include if you are in Atlanta proper, Decatur, Buckhead, Brookhaven, Sandy Springs, or an older home with unusual ductwork, crawlspace, or attic constraints.  
   - Ask for separate pricing for a conventional AC-plus-furnace option and a heat-pump option.

3. **Conditioned Air, Inc.** — good choice for North/Cobb/Fulton metro homeowners  
   - Established full-service HVAC company, especially practical for Marietta, Smyrna, Roswell, Alpharetta, Kennesaw, and surrounding areas.  
   - A useful “baseline” bid from a larger, experienced installer with ongoing maintenance capacity.  
   - Confirm exactly which equipment line and efficiency tier they are quoting rather than comparing only brand names.

4. **Estes Services** — good for broad metro coverage and straightforward replacement quotes  
   - Large Atlanta-area operation with broad scheduling capacity, HVAC service, and related plumbing/electrical capabilities.  
   - Worth including when you want a company that can handle related work such as thermostat wiring, condensate drains, electrical disconnects, or service-panel questions.  
   - Because it is a larger provider, carefully compare the proposed scope and total installed price against a more building-science-oriented bidder such as PV Heating.

5. **R.S. Andrews** — useful if the project has HVAC plus electrical/plumbing scope  
   - Another large Atlanta-area company that can be convenient if your replacement may require electrical upgrades, drain work, or other trades.  
   - Good option for a competitive quote and for homeowners who value a large service organization and maintenance-plan availability.  
   - As with any high-volume contractor, insist on a detailed scope rather than accepting a quote based solely on the size of the existing unit.

## My practical shortlist

If you only make three calls:

- **PV Heating** — technical/design-focused bid  
- **Moncrief** — established Atlanta/older-home bid  
- **Conditioned Air** or **Estes** — larger metro-service comparison bid  

That mix gives you a better chance of seeing whether one contractor is oversizing equipment, omitting duct/electrical work, or charging a premium for the same system.

## What to require from every bidder

Atlanta’s hot, humid summers make installation quality and humidity control just as important as the brand on the outdoor unit. Ask each company to provide:

- A **Manual J heating/cooling load calculation**, not just “you currently have a 3-ton unit.”  
- The exact outdoor unit, indoor coil/air handler or furnace, and thermostat model numbers.  
- The system’s **AHRI matched-system certificate** and stated **SEER2/EER2** rating.  
- Whether the quote includes duct repairs, return-air improvements, new refrigerant line set or line-set flush, condensate safety switches, drain upgrades, pad/stand, surge protection, permits, and haul-away.  
- Startup/commissioning details: refrigerant charge verification, static-pressure/airflow testing, and thermostat setup.  
- Separate warranties for **equipment**, **labor**, and any extended warranty.  
- Confirmation that the installer holds the appropriate active **Georgia Conditioned Air Contractor license** and will pull the required permit.

## One Atlanta-specific recommendation

Do not automatically replace a failed AC with another single-stage AC of the same size. Ask for a quote on a **variable-speed or two-stage heat pump** as well. In Atlanta, a properly sized heat pump can provide excellent cooling and humidity control, handle much of the winter heating load, and may be a better long-term choice than AC-only equipment—especially if your current furnace is aging.

Avoid any contractor who quotes a replacement solely from square footage or the old unit’s nameplate, pressures you to sign immediately, or cannot explain why the proposed tonnage is correct.
